title: Completion fragment metering and KV credit reporter
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Add a lightweight completion-fragment metering layer and a KV cache credit reporter that together produce per-fragment latency and cost signals. These signals will be emitted as trace hooks, Prometheus metrics, and structured JSON logs so the Console can show a breakdown of latency and inferred cost by fragment (prefix vs generated), and so billing analytics can reconcile cache savings vs raw token spend.
background: We currently surface request-level latency and coarse token counts but lack a reliable mapping between fine-grain generation work and cache savings. Engineers and SREs need visibility into which parts of a completion (prompt prefix, reused KV slices, newly generated fragments) incur GPU work, and how many effective KV credits were consumed. Product wants a dashboard that attributes latency and cost to fragments for canary rollouts and SLA investigations.
proposed_solution:
1) Introduce a Completion Fragment Annotator: at runtime, mark boundaries where generation transitions between using cached KV pages and producing new logits. Emit a trace span per fragment with tags: fragment_id, role (prefix|reused|generated), start_ns, end_ns, model_variant, seq_len, kv_hit_ratio.
2) KV Credit Reporter: hook into the KV allocator to count page reads/writes per request and expose a 'kv_credits' metric per fragment and per request.
3) Telemetry plumbing: enrich traceexporter to include the fragment spans, add two Prometheus counters/gauges (fragment_generation_ns, fragment_kv_credits) and a structured log event (json) that summarises fragments for downstream billing and dashboards.
4) Backfill shim: when new events are enabled for a model variant, emit a sample-based migration record for a small subset of traffic to validate aggregation correctness.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime emits a trace/span for each completion fragment with required tags (fragment_id, role, start_ns, end_ns, kv_hit_ratio)
Prometheus metrics fragment_generation_ns and fragment_kv_credits are available for a canary service and show non-zero values during synthetic tests
Structured JSON log per request contains an array of fragment summaries and total_kv_credits; logs validate against schema in log-consumer repo
Console dashboard prototype shows per-fragment latency and kv_credits for a selected recent window (last 6h) and can filter by model_variant and route
No latency regressions >1% p95 when feature flag enabled on canary (validated with Perf harness)
All telemetry field names documented in runtime-observability spec and reviewed by PM and SRE
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flag gated rollout: start on canary cluster (5%) for 72h. 2) Monitor telemetry volume and CPU overhead; if <2% overhead and no data correctness issues, ramp to 25% then 100% over 7 days. 3) Enable structured log export to pipeline only after 25% stage to avoid immediate storage surge. 4) Switch console to read new metrics via metrics-service feature flag and run UI A/B to validate UX.
testing_plan: Unit tests for annotator boundaries, integration test that runs synthetic request sequences covering: (a) full-prefix-only, (b) repeated-kv-hit-heavy requests, (c) fresh-generation-long requests. End-to-end test that validates Prometheus metrics and JSON log shape. Perf run with 10k synthetic requests to measure overhead. Manual verification steps documented in the PR.
notes: We must keep trace span payloads small; only include numeric tags and short identifiers to avoid trace storage blowup.
Sampling: for high-traffic routes we will sample fragments at 10% for structured logs but keep Prometheus metrics aggregated at full resolution.
Work with Billing team to map kv_credits to monetary units (separate conversion table).
Coordinate with Console infra to add a new dashboard tile for 'Fragment-level latency & KV credits' and query templates.
This should convert easily to future 'per-batch' attribution when batching changes are applied.
